posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md:
Thanks for the great link, Tom! I've always wanted to make a light-in -flight hologram as well. The first ones were done with very short coherence length laser light instead of short pulses (if I remember correctly). I was a laser tech (building C02 lasers) at Spectra-Physics when Nils did the pulsed work there in the applications lab. He was working with a fan propeller at the time. 

I just had a look at Nils' paper in the Proceedings of the International Symposium on Display Holography, Volume 2 (1985), and saw that it was a reprint of Applied Optics, Volume 22, page 215, January 15, 1983.

posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md:
There's a fairly good explanation in Nils Abramson's book, "The Making and Evaluation of Holograms" It's not in print now, as far as I know, but may still be available. I believe Colin found a copy l;ast year. ( [http://www.amazon.com/exec/obidos/ASIN/ ... 07-4245547](http://www.amazon.com/exec/obidos/ASIN/0120428202/hologramcommunic/104-2466307-4245547) )

Nils also has written a book on Light in Flight ( [http://www.amazon.com/exec/obidos/ASIN/ ... 07-4245547](http://www.amazon.com/exec/obidos/ASIN/0819421073/hologramcommunic/104-2466307-4245547) )

Have you tried contacting Nils Abramson himself. Tell him you're interested in Relativity, especially Black Holes. He's fascinated by all this!
